title: Trust and Reputation
description: Trust is the willingness to be vulnerable based on the expectation of fair behavior. Reputation is what follows you into future negotiations.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: Trust is the willingness to be vulnerable based on the expectation of fair behavior. Reputation is what follows you into future negotiations.

sections.title: How It Actually Appears
content: A negotiator known for fairness gets initial offers that are already close to reasonable because counterparts don't want to waste time with games.
Someone with a reputation for last-minute nibbling finds that counterparts pad initial offers and add 'annoyance premiums.'

sections.title: Common Trust-Building Behaviors
content: Doing what you say you will do, on time.
Admitting a small weakness or limitation early (this signals honesty).
Sharing an objective standard instead of just a demand.

sections.title: Warning Signs of Distrust
content: The other party demands extensive verification of simple claims.
They refuse to share any information that could be used against them.
They insist on penalty clauses for minor infractions.

sections.title: Protection Strategy
sections.content: Check a counterpart's reputation by asking peers in your network: 'What was it like to close a deal with them?' A three-minute call can prevent months of pain.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Your reputation for fairness is a silent partner in every future deal. Don't trade it for a short-term gain.
